datasets.name: tomorrow
queryLines:
SELECT city_name, pollutant, target_day, ROUND(100 * probability, 1) AS probability_pct,
       -- table text: the widget would print 20.00 and null, so numbers and "–" are formatted here
       coalesce(format_number(100 * probability, 1), '–') AS probability_txt,
       CASE WHEN warned THEN 'warning' WHEN status = 'ok' THEN 'no warning' ELSE 'no forecast' END AS verdict,
       run_kind, date_format(issued_at + INTERVAL 1 HOUR, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') AS issued_cet,
       coalesce(format_number(pm_d1_max_ug_m3, 0), '–') AS yesterday_ug_m3,
       coalesce(format_number(pm_d_morning_max_ug_m3, 0), '–') AS this_morning_ug_m3,
       coalesce(format_number(t_mean_c, 1), '–') AS temperature_c, coalesce(format_number(wind_mean_ms, 1), '–') AS wind_ms,
       coalesce(CAST(calm_hours AS STRING), '–') AS calm_hours, coalesce(format_number(precip_sum_mm, 1), '–') AS rain_mm,
       coalesce(unusable_reason, '–') AS unusable_reason
FROM forecast_tomorrow
WHERE target_day = (SELECT max(target_day) FROM forecast_tomorrow)
ORDER BY probability DESC

datasets.name: tomorrow_limits
queryLines:
SELECT CAST(max(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'PM10' THEN limit_ug_m3 END) AS INT) AS pm10_limit,
       CAST(max(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'PM2.5' THEN limit_ug_m3 END) AS INT) AS pm25_limit
FROM forecast_tomorrow
WHERE target_day = (SELECT max(target_day) FROM forecast_tomorrow)

datasets.name: tomorrow_summary
queryLines:
SELECT max(target_day) AS target_day, count_if(warned) AS warnings, count_if(status = 'ok') AS forecasts,
       max(run_kind) AS run_kind
FROM forecast_tomorrow
WHERE target_day = (SELECT max(target_day) FROM forecast_tomorrow)

datasets.name: updates_pm10
datasets.displayName: Tomorrow's forecast run by run – PM10

datasets.name: updates_pm25
datasets.displayName: Tomorrow's forecast run by run – PM2.5
queryLines:
SELECT city_name, run_kind, ROUND(100 * probability, 1) AS probability_pct

datasets.name: updates_table
datasets.displayName: Tomorrow's forecast runs side by side
queryLines:
SELECT target_day, city_name, pollutant,
       coalesce(format_number(100 * max(CASE WHEN run_kind = 'preliminary' THEN probability END), 1), '–')
         AS preliminary_pct,
       coalesce(format_number(100 * max(CASE WHEN run_kind = 'official' THEN probability END), 1), '–')
         AS official_pct,
       coalesce(format_number(100 * max_by(CASE WHEN run_kind = 'update' THEN probability END,
                                           CASE WHEN run_kind = 'update' THEN issued_at END), 1), '–')
         AS latest_update_pct
FROM forecast_history
WHERE target_day = (SELECT max(target_day) FROM forecast_history)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY city_name, pollutant

datasets.name: season
queryLines:

FROM measured_daily
WHERE heating_season IS NOT NULL

datasets.name: recent
queryLines:
SELECT day_cet, city_name, pollutant, ROUND(max_station_mean_ug_m3, 1) AS worst_station_ug_m3, limit_ug_m3, source
FROM measured_daily
WHERE day_cet >= date_sub(current_date(), 60)

datasets.name: verification
queryLines:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT target_day, city_name, pollutant, concat(format_number(limit_ug_m3, 0), ' µg/m³') AS daily_limit,
         concat(format_number(100 * probability, 0), '% chance') AS p,
         concat('measured ', format_number(measured_max_ug_m3, 0), ' µg/m³') AS m, outcome
  FROM forecast_verification
), verdicts AS (
  SELECT target_day, city_name, pollutant, daily_limit,
         CASE outcome
           WHEN 'hit' THEN concat('✓ smog, warned in advance (', p, ' → ', m, ')')
           WHEN 'correct_no_warning' THEN concat('✓ no smog, as forecast (', p, ' → ', m, ')')
           WHEN 'miss' THEN concat('✗ smog missed (', p, ' → ', m, ')')
           WHEN 'false_alarm' THEN concat('✗ false alarm (', p, ' → ', m, ')')
           WHEN 'pending' THEN concat('⏳ waiting for the day to end (', p, ')')
           WHEN 'no_data' THEN concat('– no valid measurement (', p, ')')
           WHEN 'no_forecast' THEN '– no forecast issued'
         END AS verdict
  FROM v
)
SELECT target_day, city_name,
       max(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'PM10' THEN daily_limit END) AS pm10_limit,
       max(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'PM10' THEN verdict END) AS pm10,
       max(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'PM2.5' THEN daily_limit END) AS pm25_limit,
       max(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'PM2.5' THEN verdict END) AS pm25
FROM verdicts
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY target_day DESC, city_name

datasets.name: verification_summary
queryLines:
SELECT pollutant,
       count_if(outcome IN ('hit', 'miss', 'false_alarm', 'correct_no_warning')) AS judged_forecasts,
       count_if(outcome = 'hit') AS hits, count_if(outcome = 'miss') AS misses,
       count_if(outcome = 'false_alarm') AS false_alarms, count_if(outcome = 'correct_no_warning') AS correct_quiet,
       ROUND(avg(squared_error), 4) AS live_brier, count_if(outcome = 'pending') AS pending
FROM forecast_verification
GROUP BY pollutant
ORDER BY pollutant

datasets.name: test_days_pm10
datasets.displayName: Test year 2025 – PM10 warnings per month
queryLines:
WITH days AS (
  SELECT CASE p.city_id WHEN 'warszawa' THEN 'Warszawa' WHEN 'krakow' THEN 'Kraków' WHEN 'wroclaw' THEN 'Wrocław' WHEN 'lodz' THEN 'Łódź' WHEN 'poznan' THEN 'Poznań' WHEN 'gdansk' THEN 'Gdańsk' WHEN 'szczecin' THEN 'Szczecin' WHEN 'bydgoszcz' THEN 'Bydgoszcz' WHEN 'lublin' THEN 'Lublin' WHEN 'bialystok' THEN 'Białystok' END AS city_name, p.pollutant, date_format(p.target_day, 'yyyy-MM') AS month, p.label, p.warned,
         b.warned AS persistence_warned
  FROM backtest_predictions p
  JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT pollutant, model FROM model_selection WHERE operational) s
    ON s.pollutant = p.pollutant AND s.model = p.model
  LEFT JOIN backtest_predictions b
    ON b.model = 'persistence' AND b.split = p.split AND b.city_id = p.city_id AND b.pollutant = p.pollutant
   AND b.target_day = p.target_day
  WHERE p.split = 'test'
)
SELECT city_name, month,
       CASE WHEN warned AND label = 1 THEN '✓ smog, warned in advance'
            WHEN label = 1 THEN '✗ smog missed'
            ELSE '✗ false alarm' END AS outcome
FROM days
WHERE pollutant = 'PM10' AND (label = 1 OR warned)
ORDER BY month, CASE WHEN warned AND label = 1 THEN 1 WHEN label = 1 THEN 2 ELSE 3 END

datasets.name: test_months
datasets.displayName: Test year 2025 – month by month, per city
queryLines:
WITH days AS (
  SELECT CASE p.city_id WHEN 'warszawa' THEN 'Warszawa' WHEN 'krakow' THEN 'Kraków' WHEN 'wroclaw' THEN 'Wrocław' WHEN 'lodz' THEN 'Łódź' WHEN 'poznan' THEN 'Poznań' WHEN 'gdansk' THEN 'Gdańsk' WHEN 'szczecin' THEN 'Szczecin' WHEN 'bydgoszcz' THEN 'Bydgoszcz' WHEN 'lublin' THEN 'Lublin' WHEN 'bialystok' THEN 'Białystok' END AS city_name, p.pollutant, date_format(p.target_day, 'yyyy-MM') AS month, p.label, p.warned,
         b.warned AS persistence_warned
  FROM backtest_predictions p
  JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT pollutant, model FROM model_selection WHERE operational) s
    ON s.pollutant = p.pollutant AND s.model = p.model
  LEFT JOIN backtest_predictions b
    ON b.model = 'persistence' AND b.split = p.split AND b.city_id = p.city_id AND b.pollutant = p.pollutant
   AND b.target_day = p.target_day
  WHERE p.split = 'test'
)
SELECT city_name, month, pollutant, CAST(sum(label) AS INT) AS smog_days, count_if(warned) AS warnings,
       CASE WHEN sum(label) = 0 THEN '–' ELSE concat(CAST(count_if(warned AND label = 1) AS INT), ' of ', CAST(sum(label) AS INT), ' (', CAST(ROUND(100 * count_if(warned AND label = 1) / sum(label)) AS INT), '%)') END AS caught,
       CASE WHEN count_if(warned) = 0 THEN '–' ELSE concat(CAST(count_if(warned AND label = 1) AS INT), ' of ', CAST(count_if(warned) AS INT), ' (', CAST(ROUND(100 * count_if(warned AND label = 1) / count_if(warned)) AS INT), '%)') END AS warnings_right,
       CASE WHEN sum(label) = 0 THEN '–' ELSE concat(CAST(count_if(persistence_warned AND label = 1) AS INT), ' of ', CAST(sum(label) AS INT), ' (', CAST(ROUND(100 * count_if(persistence_warned AND label = 1) / sum(label)) AS INT), '%)') END AS persistence_caught,
       CASE WHEN count_if(persistence_warned) = 0 THEN '–' ELSE concat(CAST(count_if(persistence_warned AND label = 1) AS INT), ' of ', CAST(count_if(persistence_warned) AS INT), ' (', CAST(ROUND(100 * count_if(persistence_warned AND label = 1) / count_if(persistence_warned)) AS INT), '%)') END AS persistence_right
FROM days
GROUP BY ALL
HAVING sum(label) > 0 OR count_if(warned) > 0 OR count_if(persistence_warned) > 0   -- quiet months: nothing to show
ORDER BY city_name, month, pollutant

datasets.name: brier_pm10

ORDER BY brier

datasets.name: reliability
queryLines:
SELECT r.pollutant, ROUND(100 * r.mean_probability, 1) AS forecast_pct,
       ROUND(100 * r.observed_frequency, 1) AS observed_pct, r.n_days
FROM reliability r
JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT pollutant, model FROM model_selection WHERE operational) s
  ON s.pollutant = r.pollutant AND s.model = r.model
WHERE r.split = 'test' AND r.n_days >= 30

datasets.name: acceptance
queryLines:
SELECT pollutant, CASE criterion WHEN 'K1' THEN 'Better than the calendar average?' WHEN 'K2' THEN 'Better than "tomorrow like today"?' WHEN 'K3' THEN 'Does "70%" really mean about 70%?' WHEN 'K4a' THEN 'Does it catch smog days?' WHEN 'K4b' THEN 'Are its warnings rarely false?' END AS test, criterion AS code, CASE criterion WHEN 'K1' THEN 'above 0' WHEN 'K2' THEN concat('below ', format_number(threshold, 4)) WHEN 'K3' THEN 'gap at most 15 pp' WHEN 'K4a' THEN 'at least 60%' WHEN 'K4b' THEN 'at most 50%' END AS required, CASE WHEN criterion IN ('K4a', 'K4b') THEN concat(format_number(100 * value, 0), '%') WHEN criterion = 'K3' THEN concat(format_number(100 * value, 1), ' pp') ELSE format_number(value, 4) END AS reached,
       CASE WHEN passed THEN '✓ passed' ELSE '✗ not passed' END AS result
FROM acceptance
UNION ALL
SELECT 'PM2.5', t.test, t.code, '–', '–', '– (PM10 only)'
FROM VALUES ('Does it catch smog days?', 'K4a'), ('Are its warnings rarely false?', 'K4b') AS t(test, code)
ORDER BY pollutant, code

datasets.name: dq
queryLines:
SELECT source,
       CASE metric WHEN 'records_received' THEN 'Records received' WHEN 'unique_readings' THEN 'Unique readings'
            WHEN 'resent_duplicates' THEN 'Re-sent duplicates (collapsed)' WHEN 'late_rejected' THEN 'Late (rejected)'
            WHEN 'quarantined' THEN 'Quarantined (total)' WHEN 'silver_readings' THEN 'Accepted readings'
            WHEN 'silver_valid' THEN 'Accepted and valid' ELSE metric END AS measure,
       metric, value, ROUND(pct_of_unique, 1) AS pct_of_unique
FROM dq_summary
ORDER BY source, metric

datasets.name: dq_reasons
queryLines:
SELECT source,
       CASE metric WHEN 'late_rejected' THEN 'late'
                   WHEN 'quarantined_missing_value' THEN 'empty value' WHEN 'quarantined_below_min' THEN 'below 0'
                   WHEN 'quarantined_above_max' THEN 'above 1000 µg/m³' WHEN 'quarantined_unknown_station' THEN 'unknown station'
                   WHEN 'flag_frozen' THEN 'flag: frozen sensor' WHEN 'flag_spike' THEN 'flag: spike'
                   WHEN 'flag_drift' THEN 'flag: drift' END AS reason,
       value
FROM dq_summary
WHERE metric IN ('late_rejected', 'quarantined_missing_value', 'quarantined_below_min', 'quarantined_above_max',
                 'quarantined_unknown_station', 'flag_frozen', 'flag_spike', 'flag_drift')

lines: # Will the daily limit be exceeded tomorrow?
Probability that the **daily mean of the worst station** in the city exceeds the limit (PM10 50 µg/m³, PM2.5 25 µg/m³). A warning is issued at 50% or more.
*What you see depends on who you are: rows by voivodeship and technical columns are filtered by Unity Catalog (schema `gold_secure`).*
**Data:** measurements – GIOŚ (Chief Inspectorate of Environmental Protection); weather forecasts – Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0).

**Run kinds**
- *preliminary* – before 11:30 CET, this morning's readings are not in yet
- *official* – first run from 11:30 CET, judged against measurements
- *update* – later run, newer weather forecast

lines: An **exceedance day**: the daily mean of the city's worst station is above the limit. Heating season = October–April. Data: GIOŚ archive 2021–2025 (verified) and the live GIOŚ feed (finished days only, not yet verified by GIOŚ). PM10 limit: at most 35 exceedance days a year.

lines:
# Did the official forecasts come true?
Each official forecast (issued at 11:30 CET the day before) next to what was measured on that day: the daily mean of the city's worst station compared with the daily limit. A warning is issued at 50% or more.
- ✓ *no smog, as forecast* – no warning, limit not exceeded
- ✓ *smog, warned in advance* – warning, limit exceeded
- ✗ *smog missed* – limit exceeded without a warning
- ✗ *false alarm* – warning, but the limit was not exceeded
- ⏳ *waiting* – the day is not over yet (judged after midnight CET)

The live record is short (the live feed started in October 2026); the test year 2025 on the Model page is the main evidence – this page shows the model keeps working on new data.

lines:
# How the model did in 2025, month by month
2025 is the test year: the model never saw it while learning, and the tests on the Model page were fixed before it was checked. Each bar counts **smog days** – days when the daily limit was exceeded (the city's worst station: PM10 above 50 µg/m³, PM2.5 above 25 µg/m³) – and **false alarms**. A warning means a forecast of 50% or more.
**All 10 cities together** (charts with City = All, and the last table): days are summed over the cities – one smog day = one city on one day (February: 28 days × 10 cities = 280 city-days).

frame.title: PM10 – smog days caught, missed, and false alarms
PM2.5 – smog days caught, missed, and false alarms

lines:
**How to read the tables** – two questions, both answered as "X of Y":
- **Smog days that got a warning** – did we miss smog? Example: 16 of 19 = of 19 smog days, 16 were warned the day before. Higher is better.
- **Warnings followed by smog** – can you trust a warning? Example: 16 of 22 = of 22 warnings, 16 were followed by a real smog day (the other 6 were false alarms). Higher is better.
- A good forecast needs **both** to be high: warning every day would catch every smog day, but most warnings would be wrong.
- **"Tomorrow like today"** – the simplest possible forecast: warn if the last full day was a smog day (when the forecast is issued at 11:30, today is not over yet, so that is yesterday). The model should do better than that.
- Why "tomorrow like today" is not enough: it is always **two days late**. It misses the first two days of every smog episode and keeps warning for two days after the smog is gone. It looks fine in long episodes (a frosty February), but when smog comes in short bursts of one or two days it never catches it. The model also looks at this morning's readings and the weather forecast, so it can warn before an episode starts.
- Our goal, set before testing: at least 60% of smog days warned, at least half of the warnings followed by smog.
- Months not shown had no smog day and no warning – the model correctly stayed quiet (e.g. May–September). A dash (–) = nothing to count.

lines: # Data quality of the live feed
*live* = GIOŚ API, *fault_replay* = demonstration with injected faults (never used by the model). Nothing is dropped silently: every set-aside reading has a reason.
